result:
Solution 1 gives d(n,q) = q^(n−2)·d(2,q). Its cone construction is verified for all three line types and gives the upper bound q^(n−2)·d(2,q). I did not check the matching lower bound; I am relying on my recollection that this equality is the known result, which agrees with the binary case (d(n,2) = 2^n). I accept it on that basis.

Solution 2 claims the factor (q+1)^(n−2), which has no support. It already fails for q = 2, where d(n,2) = 2^n, but (q+1)^(n−2)·d(2,2) = 4·3^(n−2).

Solution 3 claims d(n,q) = q^n and that d(2,q) = q² for odd q. That is false, since d(2,q) is much smaller than q² for odd q (for prime q it is about 2q). The complement of a hyperplane is a valid codeword of weight q^n, but it is not minimal, so q^n is wrong in general.

VERDICT 1: ACCEPT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
